title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors
authors: B. McCann, J. Bradbury, C. Xiong, R. Socher
before: Every word had one vector regardless of the sentence it appeared in.
problem: Bank in a river sentence and bank in a finance sentence got identical representations.
breakthrough: Take the encoder from a trained translation model and use its hidden states as context-sensitive word vectors.
why: The first workable contextual embedding, a few months before ELMo made the idea famous.
next: ELMo did the same thing from a language model instead of a translation model, and did it better.
inherits: The principle that a word's representation should depend on its context.
